A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Wavelet Attribution Method (WAM). Their complete main texts, references, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization and some inconsistent reporting.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on 1,000 ImageNet images and 400 ESC-50 audio samples, alongside randomization, robustness, and minimal-image analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and reports additional audio, volumetric, localization, and sensitivity evaluations in Tables 2–8 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The wavelet-gradient computation, input-noise smoothing, and integrated-gradient procedure remain equivalent: v1 Equations 1–3 correspond to v2 Equations 6–8. The meaningful-perturbation objective and Nadam optimization also remain, relocated to Appendix D.1. Additional wavelet explanations and benchmark implementations do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds SONYC-UST audio evaluation, labelled SONY-UST in Table 3; AdrenalMNIST3D and VesselMNIST medical-volume benchmarks; and PASCAL VOC multi-object localization. Appendix D.4 also introduces a remote-sensing distribution-shift case based on cited work. MNIST3D was already illustrated in v1, so its new quantitative results do not constitute a newly introduced dataset.

E2.justification: V2 adds Guided Backpropagation to the ImageNet comparisons and evaluates LayerCAM, LRP, and SRD against WAM in Table 5. It also introduces quantitative volume comparisons against six attribution baselines. The original image and audio comparator sets remain represented in the detailed tables.

E3.justification: New protocols include full-test-set volume evaluation with ResNet3D, EfficientNet3D, and 3D Former; decomposition-depth comparisons at J=1 and J=2; and mother-wavelet comparisons. Appendix D.2 adds Pointing Game localization across four backbones on a reported 1,456 VOC images. The original ImageNet and ESC-50 sample counts and metric definitions are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds mother-wavelet sensitivity checks, decomposition-depth analyses, a multi-object attribution case, and a remote-sensing failure analysis. The adversarial-model robustness study is retained and moved into the main text. Conversely, v1's static minimal-image sufficiency-threshold analysis and several additional randomization, volume, and audio-overlap examples are removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% confidence intervals for the 1,000-image randomization analysis in Figure 8 and use the median for Faithfulness on Spectra. V2 introduces no new repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The original ImageNet and ESC-50 numerical rows are retained in v2 Tables 3–4, while substantial new results appear elsewhere. For example, Table 8 reports ConvNext Pointing Game accuracy of 0.632 for WAMIG versus 0.528 for GradCAM. Reporting discrepancies also arise: v2 Table 1 assigns EfficientNet insertion scores 0.447 to WAMIG and 0.419 to WAMSG, reversing the assignments in v1 Table 4 and the retained v2 Table 4.

T1.justification: V2 adds Appendix B, including a completeness definition, Theorem B.1 and its proof under a differentiability assumption, and arguments for sensitivity, implementation invariance, and linearity. Section 3.1 also revises multidimensional wavelet normalization and supplies explicit discrete-transform and reconstruction equations. V1 only briefly discusses attribution axioms without these proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains unified wavelet-domain attribution explaining both where and what; v1 already claims applicability across three modalities. V2 explicitly extends the conclusion's quantitative state-of-the-art claim to volume benchmarks and adds an introduction assertion that explanations require a single backward pass. These are limited changes to otherwise retained core claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of mother-wavelet-dependent interpretation and claimed invariance, recommendations for choosing WAMIG versus WAMSG, and explanations of multi-object attribution spillover and remote-sensing noise reliance. Section 5 newly identifies direct text processing as an applicability limitation. These extend v1's interpretations and its existing point-cloud and listenable-audio limitations.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page link, identifies LATEC integration, and documents tested wavelet families and decomposition depths. However, it removes v1 Appendix A.2's Ubuntu, TITAN Xp, VRAM, and CUDA specifications and direct Zenodo data-access link. The original image-model identifiers and audio-noise pseudocode are retained in Appendix C.1.

R1.justification: The new Section 2.2 substantially revises positioning by discussing CartoonX, ShearletX, WCAM, and scattering transforms, explicitly acknowledging earlier wavelet-based explainability. V1's concept-discovery discussion and associated citations are removed. Additional references support the new theoretical discussion, evaluated baselines, datasets, and applications.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and wavelet background are extensively rewritten, and the title changes from Post-Hoc Explainability to Feature Attribution. Evaluation and results are reorganized; robustness moves into the main text, meaningful perturbation moves to the appendix, and the appendices are rebuilt around consistency checks, theory, evaluation, and applications.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, introduces a cross-modal summary table, consolidates the earlier image and audio tables, and adds several new experimental tables and figures. Retained audio and volume illustrations are rearranged, captions are expanded, and the robustness figure is relocated. Several supplementary galleries and the static minimal-image threshold figure are removed.

improvement.justification: New volume and localization evaluations address v1's limited empirical support for a unified method, while Section 2.2 remedies missing discussion of directly relevant wavelet explainers. These gains are tempered by conflicting WAM scores and labels across v2 Tables 1, 4, and 5, Table 5's μ-Fidelity of 1.151 despite its correlation definition, and removal of hardware and data-access details. The broader evidence and improved positioning therefore yield a limited net quality improvement.
